acceptance: With no setting, BenchBox applies no timeout to dsdgen, dbgen or dsqgen.
One optional setting limits all three from the command line, MCP and the Python API, shown by tests.
The owner confirmed the setting's name before it was committed.
description:
## Problem
BenchBox stops each single-query dsqgen call after a hard-coded 30 seconds (benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py, in the code since the first release, no recorded reason) and a dsqgen stream set after 300 seconds (benchbox/core/tpcds/streams.py). At large scale that stops a valid query 9 generation. Data generation (dsdgen, dbgen) has no timeout, and nothing lets a user set one. The only user-settable timeouts today, `execution.concurrent_queries.query_timeout_seconds` and `stream_timeout_seconds`, govern query execution on the platform.

## Owner decisions, 2026-11-20
"We do need to **ALLOW** a user to specify a datagen timeout even though we MUST NOT enforce a default timeout. We should also provide a rough estimate for the user about expected duration". On query generation hitting a timeout: "Why would query generation hit a timeout? That seems insane". On where it is set: "All tools have one setting. But we already have a timeout (surely?!) - why the hell do we need another one?" (answered: no existing setting covers generation). Separate pull request from #4409 (choice dialog: "Merge #4409 as it is, then a second pull request").

## Change
Remove the 30-second and 300-second defaults: with nothing set, BenchBox never stops a TPC generator. Add one optional setting, read by the command line, the MCP run tool and the Python API, that limits every TPC generator call (dsdgen, dbgen, dsqgen). When it stops a tool, the error says the user's limit was reached, for which tool, query and scale. Update the error text #4409 added, which names a 30-second limit.

## Decision gates
The setting's name was proposed to the owner as `--generation-timeout SECONDS`; the owner has not confirmed the name or whether it should live in the existing config section. Show the final name and config key to the owner before commit. No default value. No change to how any query or data is generated. The duration estimate is a separate item.

## Verification rubric
Pass: with nothing set, a stubbed generator that runs past 30 and 300 seconds is not stopped (tests for the single-query path and the stream path); with the setting, the stubbed generator is stopped and the error names the user's limit, tool, query and scale; the setting reaches dsdgen, dbgen and dsqgen from each of the three surfaces (one test per surface); the strings '30-second' and '300' limits are gone from the modules; changelog fragment.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
